items.stem: A ChatGPT-drafted post makes a specific performance claim about the product. Before scheduling, you should:

options.text: Verify the claim is substantiated and compliant, or remove it
options.rationale: Correct: unsubstantiated claims are a brand and legal risk.

options.text: Schedule it because it is engaging
options.rationale: Engagement does not excuse an unsupported claim.

options.text: Add an emoji to soften the claim
options.rationale: Cosmetic edits do not make a claim substantiated.

options.text: Publish and correct later if challenged
options.rationale: Publishing first and fixing later accepts avoidable risk.

items.explanation: Correct: unsubstantiated claims are a brand and legal risk.

items.stem: Which TWO conditions should a post meet before Buffer publishes it? (Select TWO.)

options.text: It has passed the human approval gate
options.rationale: Correct: approval is the control that keeps non-compliant posts off the channel.
Correct: disclosures are often legally required and must be on the post.

options.text: It has the most hashtags of the week
options.rationale: Hashtag count is not a quality or compliance control.

options.text: It was the fastest draft to produce
options.rationale: Speed of drafting says nothing about whether it should publish.

items.stem: What should a channel visual include to be accessible?

options.text: Descriptive alt text and sufficient contrast
options.rationale: Correct: alt text and contrast make the visual usable by more people.

options.text: The maximum amount of text that will fit
options.rationale: Dense text harms readability and accessibility.

options.text: Only decorative imagery with no description
A watermark across the whole image
options.rationale: A heavy watermark reduces legibility, not improves access.

items.explanation: Correct: alt text and contrast make the visual usable by more people.
